sentences.text: 1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and Sri Alok Kumar, who has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of the opposite party no.2 and perused the record.
The Vakalatnama is taken on record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.496 of 2023, under Section 376 of IPC, Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Jaidpur, District Barabanki.

3. sentences.text: Subsequently, in the statement under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the said version was reiterated by the victim.

4. In the light of the allegations, the submission of the Counsel for the applicant is that a mobile phone of the applicant was stolen, which was found with the victim and as a sequel to the said, the present FIR was lodged.
He draws my attention to the medical on record, which was conducted on 16.12.2023, which does not corroborate any allegation as levelled in the two statements.
No injury was observed on the body of the victim either internally or externally.

He further draws my attention to the statement of the prosecutrix recorded during trial, wherein, in the cross-examination, the victim admitted that she was in talking term with the applicant on mobile phone.
She also stated that the victim had received the monetary compensation from the Government.

5. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the informant vehemently opposed the bail prayer by arguing that the age of the victim is tentatively 13 years, although, no formal adjudication process with regard to the age has been carried out.
He further argues that in the two statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., a clear statement with regard to the rape has been levelled.
He thus argues that the bail application should be rejected.

6. Considering the submissions made at the bar; apart from the two statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the medical on record does not corroborate any of the said allegations; the FIR was lodged after two days of the incident without there being any plausible explanation for the delay coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 16.12.2023, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Ranchoo Verma @ Anupam Verma be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
